First full panel in the books, and I'll be honest with you: ApoB at 108 is the number I keep looking at. Lipids want work — triglycerides 142, HDL 44 — and vitamin D at 28 is scraping the floor. Testosterone sits mid-range at 468. Nothing scary, plenty actionable: this is a solid "before" picture. Fasting insulin 8.2 says metabolism is still cooperating. Let's build from here.

Second draw, early wins. ApoB nudged down to 102 and triglycerides to 131 — diet changes are showing up in the plumbing. Vitamin D responding to supplementation at 34. Testosterone basically unchanged at 452; energy complaints match it. Ferritin at 39 bears watching — not deficient, not comfortable either. Keep the fish oil, keep the walks.

Steady as she goes. Lipids keep drifting the right way (ApoB 96, LDL 114) and HbA1c ticked to 5.5. Testosterone still mid-4s at 487 with LH 4.8 — the clinic conversation about TRT is on the table now, and this panel is the clean baseline you'd want before starting. Everything hepatic and renal is boring, which is exactly how I like it.

First panel on testosterone therapy, and the axis did what it does: total T up to 742, free T 118, LH/FSH suppressed to 0.4/0.7 — expected on-protocol, not a problem to fix. Estradiol rose with it to 31; no symptoms logged, so we watch rather than react. Hematocrit 47.9 — up from baseline, still in range. Meanwhile the lipid story keeps improving: ApoB 93. Good draw.

Settling in. Testosterone holding at 815 and the insulin picture keeps tightening — fasting insulin 5.4, HOMA-IR territory I'm happy with. Estradiol 36 tracks the higher T like it should. Hematocrit 49.2, creeping — hydration before draws matters, and this is the marker TRT asks us to respect. ApoB 88 and hs-CRP 1: the cardiovascular file keeps getting thinner. Ferritin 37 still unimpressive.

Big panel, echo included — the heart itself reads structurally normal, EF mid-normal, atria where they should be. On the blood side: estradiol popped over range at 44. Given zero symptoms in the journal, the playbook says re-test before reaching for an AI. Hematocrit 50.1 — highest yet, still in range, donation is the friendly lever if it keeps climbing. IGF-1 rising at 205 now that tesamorelin is aboard. ApoB 84. The trend lines all point the right way.

Estradiol back inside at 38 on the re-test — patience beat the pill, as it usually does. IGF-1 at 232: tesamorelin earning its slot in the fridge. HbA1c 5.3, insulin 4.5, triglycerides 81 — the metabolic panel of a lighter man, because you are one. Ferritin 36 drifting down again; iron with vitamin C on empty-stomach mornings, and we re-check.

The headline is hematocrit at 51.4 — a hair over range, first flag of the TRT era. Not alarming, absolutely worth acting on: hydrate properly before draws, consider a donation, re-check next panel. Everything else is a victory lap — ApoB 74, HDL 56, hs-CRP 0.7. Testosterone 861 with free T 141. IGF-1 steady at 241.

Latest draw, and the "after" picture is real: ApoB 71 (down from 108 at baseline), triglycerides 72, HbA1c 5.2, hs-CRP 0.6. Hematocrit back inside at 50.8 — the donation worked. Two watch items and they're familiar: ferritin dipped to 33, just under range, so the iron protocol gets serious now; LH/FSH remain suppressed at 0.2/0.2, which is the deal we signed with TRT. Overall: this is what eighteen months of showing up looks like.

Yesterday earned a nod: 2 doses logged on schedule, recovery sitting at 59, and the scale at 186.9 lbs. Sleep came in at 6h33 — not your best week for it, but the HRV of 52 says the engine room is fine. Today's only ask from me: water before coffee.
Quiet, solid day. RHR 55, HRV 52, recovery 72 — three greens on the board. 1 workout in the log. No soda, which I noticed and appreciated. Protocol ticked along without drama.
The kind of day that builds the trend line. Weight 186.6 lbs, sleep 7h35, strain 6 — an honest day's work without borrowing from tomorrow. Doses done. I have no complaints, which you know is rare.
Recovery dipped to 61 — yesterday's strain of 13.5 plus a shorter night (7h56) will do that. Nothing structural; HRV 57 is still in your normal band. If today wants to be easy, let it be easy.
A 7h15 night, recovery 69, and the weekly weigh-in trend still pointing gently down at 187.4 lbs. 1 workout in the log. The streak is doing the quiet compounding work. Keep feeding it.
Logged everything, lifted nothing (rest day), kept the sodas at 0. RHR 54 continues its slow drift down — that's months of zone 2 talking, not luck. Strain 6.1, recovery 69. Carry on.
Yesterday: 0 doses, 1 soda, sleep 6h45, recovery 70. The numbers are so steady lately that my job is mostly narration. Weight 187 lbs. See you at the next draw.

Week in review: 11 doses, 4 workouts, 2 sodas, and the scale closing at 187 lbs (+0.1 lbs on the week). Average recovery 65 on 7h15 of sleep a night — the machine is humming. BP averaged 119/76. My note for next week is the same as this week: nothing heroic, just attendance.

Another week banked. Weight 187.4 lbs, +0.2 lbs on the week — the GLP-1 era continues to be quietly ruthless. 4 sessions, average strain 7.5, and recovery holding at 67. Soda count: 3. I remember when that number had two digits a week. Growth.

Strong week. 5 workouts against an average recovery of 62 — load and recovery are actually talking to each other now. BP averaging 117/77, which would make your first lab draw blush. 10 doses, all on schedule. The consistency is the protocol.
